abstract: Agent-based models of the tumor microenvironment (TME) traditionally rely on hand-coded rules that cannot generalize beyond their programmed logic. Here we present CELLSWARM, a framework that replaces rule-based cell decision-making with large language model (LLM)-driven autonomous agents. Each simulated cell maintains persistent state, 14 signal pathways, and a memory stream, with an LLM serving as its cognitive core. Using structured knowledge bases for cancer-specific context, CELLSWARM recapitulates TNBC microenvironment composition with fidelity comparable to hand-coded rules (Jensen-Shannon divergence 0.144 vs. 0.146; P=0.012 vs. random, Mann-Whitney U test). Beyond matching rule-based performance, LLM-driven agents demonstrate three capabilities absent from rule-based models: cross-cancer generalization by swapping knowledge base entries, treatment response prediction concordant with clinical data (anti-PD-1: 17.6% simulated vs. 21% clinical), and sensing of indirect genetic perturbations that propagate through intermediate signaling cascades (IFN-{gamma} KO: Agent +15.7% vs. Rules +0.3%; P=0.005). CELLSWARM demonstrates that LLM-driven cell agents can recapitulate and extend TME simulation beyond the reach of hand-coded rules.
